claims.text: Yes, the contract caps i-on's liability. Under the Limitation of Liability clause, i-on's liability for damages to the Customer, for any cause and under any form of action, is limited to one month's fees plus the remaining portion of any prepaid fees.

citations.quote: i-on's liability for damages to the Customer for any cause whatsoever, regardless of the form of action, and whether in contract or in tort, including negligence, shall be limited to one (1) month's fees and the remaining portion of any prepaid fees.

claims.text: The clause expressly excludes lost profits and other consequential damages. i-on will not be liable for them under any circumstances, even if i-on was advised of the possibility of such damages.

citations.quote: i-on will not be liable under any circumstances for any lost profits or other consequential damages, even if i-on has been advised as to the possibility of such damages.

claims.text: The sources do not list any exceptions or carve-outs from the monetary cap itself (for example, for indemnification or gross negligence). The cap is stated to apply to damages for any cause whatsoever.

citations.quote: for damages to the Customer for any cause whatsoever, regardless of the form of action

claims.text: Separately from the cap, the Customer agrees to hold i-on harmless for service interruptions outside i-on's described responsibilities, and for data loss provided i-on maintains reasonable steps to protect against it. These are risk allocations in the Conditions of Service, not stated exclusions from the cap.

citations.quote: agrees to hold i-on harmless for any interruptions in service to the Hosted Site or inability for users to reach or effectively use the Hosted Site that arises outside the scope of i-on's responsibilities as explicitly described in this Agreement.
provided that i-on maintains reasonable steps as described in this Agreement to protect against such data loss.
